en: that's what matters to the lot of us.
note: follows #9439 (slice 117) 'Forget world peace, a crust of bread,'.

en: The moment she was born, my husband went
off somewhere. Ever since, all on my own,
note: mirrors #9365/#9366 (slice 117); #9367 'I've been raising her, and yet...' follows.

en: Honestly, there's nothing sweet about her.
If you had a kid of your own
note: followed by three pause dots, then #9445 on a new line: 'If you had kids of your own...'

en: Ah, not that you'd understand, I suppose.
If I'd been born into money like you,
would I have been any happier, I wonder?
What sort of work do you do?
But, well, if you come by where I work,
I'm Martha. A factory hand,
note: pause, then #9451 on the same line.

en: and dirt poor.
note: used only after a pause: leading space (as slice 117 does).

en: Your orders, please...
I'm just off to work at the factory.
As you get older, work only gets harder
to bear...
But I can't live without working,
so there's nothing for it.
I must count myself lucky just to
have a job at all.
Are you off to work as well?
Hard at work every morning, I see.
where is it you work, exactly?
My name is Rhoda. I work at the factory.
Now that I'm older, factory work
has come to feel harder and harder,
note: #9464/#9465 shared with msg 361736, where #9523 (slice 119) 'these days...' follows the comma.

en: I'm afraid...
Still, having a job at all makes me
one of the lucky ones, I suppose.
Oh, we were so busy at work today.
I'll be worn out once I get home.
I'd like to play with Jill, too, but...
When work allows, I so look forward to
playing with a child who lives nearby.
My, my, a visitor! How unusual.
This is where the factory women live.
What brings you to an old woman like me?
Have you got the wrong room, perhaps?
Hoho. If an old woman like me will do,
please come and visit again.
Oh, work was hard today.
Things I never minded when I was young
have become a strain...
Nobody wants to grow old, do they?
You're still so young...
You must be in your working prime.
It's a cold room, but please make
yourself at home.
How nice of you to come and visit
an old woman like me.
I'm Rhoda. I work at this factory.
This is the factory where I work.
Is there something you need?
Oh, working in the same position all day
really makes my back ache.
Oh, hello.
Does someone in your family work here?
I lost all my children
long ago...
I've been alone ever since.
Maybe that's why I'm so fond of children.
I so look forward to playing with
a little girl who lives nearby.
Say, have you heard?
About the murders in this city lately...
Haven't they caught the killer yet?
I do worry the children might be attacked.
Now, an old woman like me, it wouldn't
really matter if I were attacked.
The serial killer, they say,
is called "Jack the Ripper"
by the people in town.
If you ask me, the killer is surely
someone who was never loved as a child.
The value of life is something we learn
through love.
Many criminals of the past who were never
loved are proof of that.
Living all alone is hard...
You seem a lonely soul as well.
